expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "Your test would have passed on all 21 days of the incident. The table wasn't empty. It was full of rows whose value was 0."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "The COALESCE(x, 0) is the actual hazard. It converts unknown into a legal, plausible, silently-wrong value — the data equivalent of except: pass."

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation on revenue — sum the warehouse against the source of truth, daily. This is the only one of the four that catches logic errors."

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "Build to staging → assert → promote on pass. If tests run after publish, bad numbers reach finance regardless of how good the tests are."

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Contract at the boundary. Select columns explicitly so an upstream rename errors instead of yielding nulls."

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Assert the null rate before coalescing... null_rate(amount) < threshold fails the build."

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Names it explicitly ("Three weeks of silence is a UI failure too") but proposes visibility as the fix (surfacing timestamps), not detection prevention

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: "Nulls were your signal and you erased them before anything could look... a wrong join produces perfectly well-shaped wrong data."
